function: Uplink massive MIMO symbol detection: deep-unfolded Broyden and BFGS quasi-Newton iterations (Broyden-Net, BFGS-NetS, BFGS-NetV) replace MMSE matrix inversion (p. 2-3).
system: Uplink massive MIMO: BS with P receive antennas, K single-antenna users, (K,P) = (32,64), (16,128), (32,128); BPSK and 16QAM; no RIS; band not stated (p. 1, 4).
method: Deep unfolding of Broyden/BFGS quasi-Newton iterations with trainable scalar or vector parameters and SoftS activation; supervised MSE loss on random symbols; one network per setting (p. 2-4).
data_channel: Own simulator: i.i.d. Rayleigh and Kronecker spatially correlated channels, from [10], [11]; random symbols, SNR drawn in 0-16 dB; no standard or measured data (p. 3-4).
test_conditions: Matched: each network trained and tested with the same channel, modulation, and antenna size; SNR 0-16 dB, 2000 tests per SNR; mismatch is future work (p. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: MMSE and BFGS. Learned: LcgNet and OAMP-Net (p. 3).
metrics: Symbol error rate versus SNR for BPSK and 16QAM; SER versus number of layers at 14 dB; multiplication counts (p. 4-5).
complexity: Table II: multiplications, Broyden-Net 8K^2+4K+L(36K^2+16K), BFGS-Net 8K^2+4K+L(16K^2+6K), MMSE 8K^3+4K^2; O(K^2) versus O(K^3) (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 3: "the Kronecker model presented in Eq. (18) is used to describe this MIMO channel"; the Rayleigh channel "obeys an independent and identical Gaussian distribution". Custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "During training and testing, match conditions were used for channel models and modulation orders for each experiment"; p. 5: "The next step will be to explore the detection performance under channel and modulation mode mismatch".
q3_support: p. 3: "traditional linear method MMSE, Quasi-Newton method BFGS, and DL methods LcgNet and OAMP-Net algorithms"; SER curves in Figs. 4-6 (p. 4) compare all of them.
q4_support: p. 5: "A comparison of the complexity of the different detection scheme under 16QAM modulation is shown in the Table II"; Table II lists multiplication counts for each scheme.
q5_support: p. 4: "The data of training and testing are generated from the corresponding set of constellations". Self-generated data; no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Area 1: deep-unfolded quasi-Newton detectors. Tables I and II are images and were read on PDF pages 4 and 5. OAMP-Net is left out of Table II as too complex (p. 5) and has the best accuracy in Fig. 6 (p. 5).
